rv.q: A revival that is playing the Hollywood Pantages Theatre is an electrifying and exhilarating rock opera that will dazzle your senses.

THE WHO'S TOMMY The Musical's timeless themes of love, alienation, and the perils of hero-worship, along with its hit songs, exciting choreography, and marvelous performances, make this rockin’ revival one worth experiencing.
The latest tour gives the show an incoherency that leaves even fans lost and unaffected.
This revved-up version of "Tommy" doesn't settle for drawing on '60s nostalgia.
A spectacular production design, mesmerizing choreography, and soaring vocals add up to a thrilling theatrical extravaganza at the Hollywood Pantages.

The North American tour of Pete Townshend and Des McAnuff's rock opera, now playing at the Hollywood Pantages Theatre through November 15th, brings the familiar score to a visually arresting production whose theatrical ingenuity does not always translate into emotional resonance.
It is ultimately an entertaining evening if approached as a rock concert, even though the story itself is lost in the noise.
Unfortunately, it's disappointing to see how much emotional resonance and story comprehension seem to have been lost between the Broadway revival and the National Tour.
If you consider yourself a Wholigan, “The Who's TOMMY” might scratch a nostalgic itch.

cn.t: Critics are split on this Tommy tour: stunning visuals, choreography, and iconic rock score earn praise, but some find the streamlined one-act road version sacrifices narrative coherence. Ideal for Wholigans; casual theatergoers may find it spectacle over substance.
